game.title: Pokémon Unbound
game.revision_note: Codes are tied to specific Unbound releases — a code verified on 2.1.1.1 may fail or misbehave on other versions. Most codes here were hand-verified on 2.1.1.1 (including on Delta).
warnings: Enable ONE cheat at a time — stacking cheats is the most common cause of freezes and save corruption in Unbound.
Unbound has deliberate anti-cheat: spawning protected or story items can force-restart the game.
Classic FireRed PC-item codes (82003884…) are broken here — items can't be withdrawn or reset the game. Use the Cube codes below instead.
No working Walk Through Walls code exists for Unbound — FireRed WTW codes are incompatible.
Avoid 'Unlock All Badges' codes — they can permanently break gym leader battles.
Back up your .sav before enabling anything, and never save while a glitch is on screen.

codes.name: Master Code
codes.description: Must be entered and enabled before any item or modifier code will work.

codes.name: Rare Candies via Cube V3
codes.description: Replaces the Poké Balls in the Cube V3's Poké Balls pocket with Rare Candies. This is the working replacement for the broken classic PC candy code.
codes.activation: Open Cube V3 → Poké Balls. Candies show quantity 0 but work: give one to each party Pokémon as a held item, then Take them back — they land in the Items pocket as usable candies.
side_effects: Replaces the Poké Balls currently in that Cube slot.
Uses the same slot as the Master Ball Cube code — enable only one at a time.

codes.name: Master Balls via Cube
codes.description: Converts the Poké Balls in the first Cube slot into Master Balls. Replacement for the broken classic PC Master Ball code, which resets the game.
codes.activation: Enable, then check the first Poké Ball slot in your Cube
side_effects: Overwrites the Poké Balls in that slot.
Uses the same slot as the Rare Candy Cube code — enable only one at a time.

codes.name: Unlimited Money
codes.activation: Enable, then check your money at a Poké Mart

codes.name: Unlimited Money (CodeBreaker alternative)
codes.description: Sets money to a huge fixed value. Note: a 999F variant of the second line circulates for v2.0 — on 2.1.x use this 000F version.

codes.name: Shiny Wild Pokémon
codes.description: Forces wild Pokémon to be shiny while keeping stats, gender and ability rolled normally (unlike the old 2-line shiny code, which is broken in Unbound).
codes.activation: Enable before entering a wild encounter
side_effects: Caught Pokémon register as obtained via trade — they stop obeying past the current level cap.
Turn the code off after catching; the effect has been reported to stick on some emulators.

codes.name: EXP section Master Code
codes.description: Dedicated master block for the Unlimited EXP cheat — this is its OWN master code, separate from the main Master Code. Add as its own cheat.

codes.name: Unlimited EXP
codes.description: Defeated Pokémon yield unlimited EXP while enabled. Requires the EXP section master code (not the main Master Code).
codes.activation: Defeat a Pokémon; disable the cheat to stop gaining
side_effects: Emulator-sensitive — multiple RetroArch users report it not working; verified elsewhere.

codes.name: Infinite EXP (hold R)
codes.description: After a KO, hold R to pump EXP continuously; release to stop.
codes.activation: Hold R after defeating a Pokémon; release to stop
side_effects: Overleveling past Unbound's level caps makes Pokémon disobey.

codes.name: Sell Items at High Prices
codes.description: Items sell to the Poké Mart at inflated prices — a money route that avoids the direct money codes.
codes.activation: Enable, then sell any item at a Poké Mart

codes.name: Poké Mart Items Cost $1
codes.description: Everything at the Poké Mart costs 1 Pokédollar.
codes.activation: Enable, then buy at any Poké Mart
side_effects: One report of mart purchases glitching after the second gym badge when item cheats are active — keep purchases modest and back up saves.
